instruction: Bucket {{reference-architectures-S3-eventnotif-us-east-1-BucketName}} is supposed to route ObjectCreated events under CategoryA/* to queue {{reference-architectures-S3-eventnotif-us-east-1-QueueName}} and under CategoryB/* to topic {{reference-architectures-S3-eventnotif-us-east-1-TopicName}}. Both CloudFormation custom resources that set up those notifications (SampleBucketNotificationA, SampleBucketNotificationB) show CREATE_COMPLETE. But when we upload a test file to `CategoryA/test.csv`, the SQS queue never receives a message. Where is the break?
expected_answer: The bucket actually has ZERO notification configurations deployed, even though both custom resources report CREATE_COMPLETE. The break is a bug in the custom NotificationManager Lambda that installs the notifications. Running `aws s3api get-bucket-notification-configuration --bucket {{reference-architectures-S3-eventnotif-us-east-1-BucketName}}` returns empty output, no QueueConfigurations, no TopicConfigurations, no LambdaFunctionConfigurations. Without a notification configuration S3 never even attempts to deliver anything, so permissions (which are correct: the SQS queue policy allows s3.amazonaws.com:SendMessage with aws:SourceArn=<bucket>, and the SNS topic policy allows sns:Publish the same way) never come into play. The root cause is in the NotificationManager custom resource handler ({{reference-architectures-S3-eventnotif-us-east-1-FunctionName}}). Its mergeConfigurations function is: for each key in Object.entries(currentConfig): copy value, then if inputConfig[key] exists concat it. At first deploy, the bucket had no prior notification configuration. S3 returns an empty object from GetBucketNotificationConfiguration. Object.entries of that empty object yields no iterations, so mergedConfig stays `{}` regardless of what's in inputConfig (which contained the new QueueConfiguration/TopicConfiguration). The handler then calls PutBucketNotificationConfiguration with an empty body, CloudWatch logs a `newConfiguration: {}` entry, and the custom resource returns PhysicalResourceId normally, so CloudFormation marks it CREATE_COMPLETE and the stack succeeds. The second custom resource (SampleBucketNotificationB) then runs against the same empty current config and does the same thing. Net effect: bucket notifications are never installed despite a clean stack. Fix is either to seed mergedConfig from inputConfig's keys too (so keys present only in the new input still get applied) or to switch to the native CDK/CFN bucket notification (which uses a different merge strategy).
